**Metrics (paras 194, 197):** key risk and performance indicators, including the **extent of user awareness training**; staff awareness may be part of assessing preparedness.

**IS audit (paras 224-229):** the Audit Committee oversees IS audit; it approves the IS audit policy and reviews it at least annually; audit planning is risk-based.

cards.title: Sixty-one per cent
cards.setting: CISO's office, two weeks before the examination.

lines.text: Here's our awareness dashboard. Sixty-one per cent of lower and middle managers completed this year's cyber training. Forty new recruits from September haven't done the awareness module at all.
My managers say the module is boring and the deadlines keep slipping.
And the two new directors haven't had their annual IT and cyber training.
Could we just show the examiners the training calendar? It looks very complete.

cards.title: Getting ready for the examiners
cards.situation: Two weeks before RBI's IT examination, only 61% of managers have done their annual cyber training, 40 new recruits have not had awareness training, and two new directors are untrained. What should the CISO's office do?

choices.text: Run catch-up sessions now, report the gaps and the plan to the ISC and ITSC, and show examiners accurate completion data with dates and a fix plan.
choices.outcome: Best. RBI's Directions make these trainings mandatory and expect awareness to be measured. Honest data with a dated remediation plan, overseen by the committees, shows a working programme. Hiding gaps risks a finding on governance as well.

choices.text: Show the training calendar only, since it proves training is planned.
choices.outcome: A calendar is not evidence of completion. Examiners will ask for records, and an incomplete picture damages trust.

choices.text: Train the directors first and leave staff for next year, since the Board matters most to RBI.
choices.outcome: Directors' training matters, but new recruit awareness and annual management training are mandatory too. Fix all three.

choices.text: Ask managers to tick a box confirming they have read the cyber policy instead of training.
choices.outcome: A tick box is not a training programme, and recording it as training would be misleading.

cards.title: RBI enforcement on cyber failings
cards.caption: From RBI press releases. All five actions applied the earlier cyber security framework, now replaced by the 2026 Directions.

items.label: BBK India, 2022
items.detail: Undetected intrusion; no SOC, MFA or CCMP

items.label: Tamilnad Mercantile, 2021
items.detail: Gaps found from its own incident reports

items.label: Corporation Bank, 2019
items.detail: Cancelled debit card fraud; cyber and fraud rules

items.label: Union Bank of India, 2019
items.detail: After fraudulent SWIFT messages in 2016

items.label: Kotak Mahindra Bank
items.detail: Online onboarding and new cards stopped; lifted Feb 2025

cards.title: How often?
cards.prompt: Sort each duty by the minimum frequency in RBI's 2026 Directions.

items.text: ITSC meeting
CISO's review of cyber preparedness to the Board, RMCB or ITSC
Status of VA/PT findings to the ITSC and ISC
DR drill for critical information systems
Vulnerability assessment of critical customer-facing systems
Penetration test of critical customer-facing systems
Training for Board members and senior management
Review of the digital payment products policy
Review of the IS audit policy by the Audit Committee

cards.title: What fraud control staff must learn

cards.back: How to use the bank's fraud detection systems properly.
Investigative techniques and procedures for suspected frauds.
How to set and update fraud rules, monitor exceptions continuously and act promptly.
How to tell genuine alerts apart from false positives, and escalate when needed.
How to teach cardholders and merchants to prevent fraud.
Card scheme rules, data analysis and liaison with law enforcement agencies.

cards.question: Joseph's app team wants to keep two older mobile app versions live for another year. What do the Digital Payment Security Controls Directions say?
options: Older versions may stay live as long as customers still use them
Older versions must be deactivated in a phased but time-bound way, within six months of the newer version's release
Older versions must be switched off the same day a new one is released
Older versions may stay for two years if the ITSC agrees
cards.explanation: Paragraph 68(2)(iii) requires phasing out older versions within six months of the new release, so only one version is maintained per platform apart from the overlap.

cards.title: Real case: Kotak Mahindra Bank's road back, 2025
cards.body:
After RBI's April 2024 restrictions, Kotak Mahindra Bank started **remedial measures** and sent RBI its compliances. It also commissioned an **external audit, with RBI's prior approval**, to validate them.

On **12 February 2025** RBI said it was satisfied with the submissions and remedial steps and **lifted the restrictions** on online and mobile onboarding of new customers and on issuing new credit cards.

**What examiners look for, in this and other RBI cases:**

- corrective action plans that are **complete, accurate and sustained**, not just submitted
- governance that owns IT and cyber risk at Board level
- evidence, such as independent audit, that controls really work

**Lesson:** you earn trust back with proof, not promises.

cards.title: Examiner's Citadel: what to carry forward
items: Digital payments need MFA with a dynamic or non-replicable factor, meaningful alerts, failed-login limits and reconciliation within 24 hours.
Fraud control staff are trained in tools, investigation, rule setting and false positives; customers must go through safe-usage guidance.
Board members and senior management receive annual IT and cyber training and quarterly reviews from the CISO.
Critical customer-facing systems get VA every six months and PT every year, with quarterly reporting on closure.
Awareness is measured. Accurate completion data and a dated fix plan beat a polished calendar.

cards.prompt: If an RBI examiner asked you tomorrow to prove you completed your cyber training and know how to report an incident, what evidence could you show? What would you change in your bank's programme?

quiz.question: Under the Digital Payment Security Controls Directions, which events must trigger MFA and alerts to the customer?
options: Only logins from a new device
Only transactions flagged by the fraud system
Only payments above ₹50,000 that are made from outside India or to a new overseas account
Payments, beneficiary changes, account detail changes and limit changes
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 46 requires MFA and alerts for all payment transactions (debits and credits), new or changed beneficiaries, changes in account details and revisions to transfer limits.

quiz.question: What must transaction alerts and OTPs for online purchases show, where applicable?
options: The customer's full card number
The bank's branch code
The merchant's name rather than the payment aggregator's
The customer's account balance
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 47 requires alerts and OTPs to identify the merchant name, where applicable, instead of the payment aggregator through which the payment was made.

quiz.question: How quickly must digital payment transactions be reconciled with stakeholders such as payment system operators and card networks?
options: Real-time or near-real-time, no later than 24 hours from receiving settlement files
At the end of each month
Within 48 hours of the customer's complaint
Within seven days of the transaction
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 57 sets a real-time or near-real-time reconciliation framework, not later than 24 hours from receipt of settlement files, to help detect suspicious transactions.

quiz.question: Which training must the Board receive under paragraph 204 of the Cybersecurity Directions?
options: No training, only quarterly briefings by the CISO
Training once every three years, aligned with the director's term of appointment on the Board
Annual training for all Board members on IT and cyber risks and evolving good practice
A one-time induction session only for the ITSC chair
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 204 requires annual training for all Board members and senior management, plus periodic sensitisation to technology and cyber developments.

quiz.question: For critical systems and customer-facing systems in the DMZ, how often must VA and PT be carried out at a minimum?
options: VA every six months and PT every 12 months
VA every month and PT every six months
VA and PT every quarter
VA every year and PT every two years
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 151 sets VA at least once every six months and PT at least once every 12 months for these systems; non-critical systems follow a risk-based approach.

quiz.question: Two weeks before an RBI IT examination, awareness completion is low. Which approach best fits RBI's expectations?
options: Close gaps fast, tell the committees and show accurate data with a plan
Record directors' and managers' policy read-receipts as completed cyber training for the examiners
Show examiners only the planned training calendar
Postpone new-recruit training to next year's cycle
quiz.explanation: RBI requires the trainings and expects banks to evaluate awareness. Accurate records and committee oversight of a remediation plan show a working programme; presenting plans or read-receipts as completions misleads.

quiz.question: Which of these must the bank teach fraud control staff under paragraph 55 of the Digital Payment Security Controls Directions?
options: Selling credit cards to merchants
Writing the bank's IS audit policy
Designing the bank's annual marketing campaigns
Setting and updating fraud rules and telling false positives from genuine alerts
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 55 lists fraud control tools, investigation, cardholder and merchant education, scheme rules, data analysis and law enforcement liaison, and rule setting, monitoring, escalation and false positive skills.

quiz.question: Who approves the bank's IS audit policy and how often is it reviewed?
options: RBI's regional office, once at the time of licensing and again whenever the bank changes its auditor
The Audit Committee of the Board, at least annually
The CISO, every quarter
The Head of IT, every two years
quiz.explanation: Paragraphs 224-225 give the Audit Committee oversight of IS audit; it approves the IS audit policy and reviews it at least annually.

quiz.question: A customer's mobile banking app is installed on a second phone. What must the bank do under the device binding rules?
options: Notify the customer on several channels and keep a record of devices
Allow it silently because the password was correct
Ask the customer to visit the branch with both phones within a week, or the app will be blocked
Block the second phone without telling the customer
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 68(6) requires device binding; where multiple devices are allowed, the customer is notified of each new registration on several channels and can disable registered devices.

quiz.question: What led RBI to lift Kotak Mahindra Bank's restrictions in February 2025?
options: Remedial measures and compliances validated by an external audit approved by RBI in advance
Payment of a monetary penalty in place of the restrictions
A court order directing RBI to lift the restrictions
A change in RBI's cybersecurity rules that removed the original requirements the bank had failed to meet
quiz.explanation: RBI's February 2025 press release says the bank undertook remedial measures, submitted compliances and commissioned an RBI-approved external audit, after which RBI lifted the restrictions.

references.title: Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks – Cybersecurity, Technology: Risk, Resilience and Assurance Framework) Directions, 2026
references.note: Security policies must be communicated to staff, vendors and partners with education on cyber risks; key roles get targeted training; suspicious behaviour is reported to the incident team; awareness is evaluated periodically; awareness is mandatory for all new recruits, with annual training for lower and middle management and for all Board members and senior management.

references.title: Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks – Cybersecurity, Technology: Risk, Resilience and Assurance Framework) Directions, 2026
references.provision: Paragraphs 7-28 (Board policies, ITSC, IT Steering Committee, ISC, Head of IT, CISO)
references.note: The Board approves IT, information security and cybersecurity policies, reviewed at least annually; the ITSC and IT Steering Committee meet at least quarterly; the ISC approves awareness initiatives; the CISO is independent of the Head of IT and reports cyber preparedness at least quarterly.

references.title: Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks – Cybersecurity, Technology: Risk, Resilience and Assurance Framework) Directions, 2026
references.provision: Paragraphs 42-43, 117-120, 148, 193 and 205-207 (acceptable use; secure mail; anti-phishing; customer education)
references.note: Staff and service providers must follow acceptable-use policies; mail systems must resist spoofing and look-alike domains with DMARC; banks subscribe to anti-phishing and anti-rogue app takedown services and teach customers never to share credentials, OTPs or PINs.

references.title: Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks – Cybersecurity, Technology: Risk, Resilience and Assurance Framework) Directions, 2026
references.provision: Paragraphs 47-54 and 104-125, 135 (data leak prevention; user access; teleworking; removable media; vendor staff)
references.note: Access only for a valid business need, least privilege, no admin rights on end-user machines, mandatory MFA for privileged users of critical systems, dormant accounts disabled, removable media blocked unless authorised, and a data leak prevention strategy covering vendors.

references.title: Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks – Cybersecurity, Technology: Risk, Resilience and Assurance Framework) Directions, 2026
references.provision: Paragraphs 165-193 and 221-223 (DR drills; incident response; DAKSH reporting; CCMP; CSOC staff)
references.note: Incident response policy and specialised training for incident handlers; cyber incidents reported to RBI on DAKSH within six hours of detection with CERT-In notified proactively; a Cyber Crisis Management Plan; half-yearly DR drills for critical systems; trained CSOC staff.

references.title: Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks – Cybersecurity, Technology: Risk, Resilience and Assurance Framework) Directions, 2026
references.provision: Paragraphs 151, 161, 194-197 and 224-230 (VA/PT; metrics; IS audit; repeal)
references.note: VA at least every six months and PT at least every 12 months for critical and customer-facing DMZ systems, quarterly closure status to the ITSC and ISC, metrics including awareness, IS audit under the Audit Committee, and repeal of the earlier cybersecurity framework.

references.title: Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks – Digital Payment Security Controls) Directions, 2026
references.provision: Paragraphs 7-9, 40-58, 64-68 (policy; authentication; fraud monitoring; staff training; customer education; app controls)
references.note: Board-approved digital payment policy reviewed annually; MFA with at least one dynamic or non-replicable factor; alerts; failed-login limits; fraud rules and staff fraud training; reconciliation within 24 hours; mandatory secure-usage guidance for customers; device binding.

references.title: Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks – Know Your Customer) Directions, 2025
references.provision: Paragraph 63 (secrecy obligations and sharing of information)
references.note: Customer information from the banking relationship must be kept secret, and account-opening data must not be used for cross-selling or other purposes without the customer's express permission.

references.title: Supervisory Action against Kotak Mahindra Bank Limited under Section 35A of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949 (press release, 24 April 2024)
references.note: RBI stopped online and mobile onboarding of new customers and new credit cards after IT examinations found deficiencies in inventory, patch and change, access, vendor risk, data leak prevention and BCP/DR; lifted on 12 February 2025.

references.title: RBI imposes monetary penalty on Bank of Bahrain & Kuwait BSC, India Operations (press release, 19 December 2022)
references.note: A penalty of ₹2.66 crore for cyber security framework failures, including no SOC, no MFA for critical servers, admin rights on endpoints, missing logs and no Cyber Crisis Management Plan, which let an intrusion go undetected.

references.title: Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023
references.note: Sets duties for data fiduciaries such as banks, including reasonable security safeguards and breach notification; the DPDP Rules, 2025 apply in phases. The official text blocks automated access and was not opened, so the quest covers it only in general terms.

references.title: CERT-In Directions under section 70B(6) of the IT Act, 2000 (28 April 2022)
references.note: CERT-In's own directions set cyber incident reporting duties for body corporates including banks. The host refuses automated connections, so the text was not opened and the quest does not state its details.

bank.question: A local area bank's IT head says RBI's 2026 Cybersecurity Directions for commercial banks now bind his bank too. Is he right?
options: Yes, but only for its Board-approved cybersecurity policy chapter
No; the Directions cover only foreign banks operating in India
No; local area banks are outside the definition used by these Directions
Yes; every bank licensed by RBI, of whatever type, became a commercial bank on 31 July 2026
bank.explanation: The Directions apply to banking companies other than small finance, payments and local area banks, plus corresponding new banks and SBI. Foreign bank branches are covered with some comply-or-explain flexibility.

bank.question: A foreign bank's Indian branches want to depart from a paragraph in Chapter IV of the Directions. On what basis can they do so?
options: Under 'comply or explain', if RBI accepts a reasonable justification
Only with a resolution of the Indian country management committee
Automatically, because foreign banks follow only their home regulator's cyber rules for branches
Never; foreign branches must follow every paragraph without exception
bank.explanation: Foreign banks in branch mode may follow a comply-or-explain approach for Chapters II, III, IV and VII and selected Chapter V paragraphs, but deviations need RBI to accept a reasonably justifiable explanation.

bank.question: The Board wants to delegate approval of a major rewrite of the Cybersecurity Policy entirely to the ITSC. What do the Directions allow?
options: The ITSC may review the policy, but material amendments must still be approved by the Board
Only RBI may approve material amendments to a bank's cyber policy
The CISO may approve the rewrite if the ITSC chair agrees
The ITSC may approve any change, including material ones, because delegation by the Board is unlimited
bank.explanation: Paragraph 8 allows the Board to delegate review to the ITSC, but material amendments must be approved by the Board, and the review takes place at least annually.

bank.question: Which statement about the bank's Cybersecurity Policy is correct under paragraph 15?
options: It is Board-approved and separate from the IT and information security policies
It may be a short annex inside the IT policy, approved by the Head of IT without going to the Board
It replaces the information security policy entirely
It is optional for banks with an ISO 27001 certificate
bank.explanation: Paragraph 15 requires a Board-approved Cybersecurity Policy that is distinct and separate from the IT and information security policies, so that cyber risks and their mitigation stand out.

bank.question: The ISC at Godavari Harbour Bank is to be chaired by the Head of IT. Which requirement does this break?
options: The ISC must be chaired by an independent director with at least seven years of IT experience
The ISC must be chaired by an RBI nominee
The ISC's head must come from the risk management vertical
The ISC must be chaired by the managing director
bank.explanation: Paragraph 23 places the ISC under the ITSC's oversight, includes the CISO and representatives of business and IT, and requires the head of the ISC to be from risk management.

bank.question: Which duty belongs to senior management under paragraph 20 of the Directions?
options: Chairing the ITSC and setting its quarterly agenda
Creating a culture of IT risk awareness and cyber hygiene through IT risk management processes
Performing the IS audit of the CISO's office
Approving the bank's licence to offer digital payments
bank.explanation: Paragraph 20 requires senior management to execute the IT strategy and ensure IT risk processes create a culture of IT risk awareness and cyber hygiene, with a robust cyber posture.

bank.question: A vendor's support engineers use the bank's ticketing system and see customer names. What does paragraph 199 expect for them?
options: The bank communicates its security policies to them and educates them on cyber risks
Nothing, because vendor staff are the vendor's responsibility alone once the outsourcing contract is signed
Only a clause in the contract, without any communication
Full annual Board-level cyber training
bank.explanation: Paragraph 199 covers users, employees, vendors and partners: the bank must communicate its security and acceptable-use policies, including for customer data, and educate them about cyber risks and protection.

bank.question: Which group must receive targeted awareness and training under paragraph 200?
options: Only customers using internet banking for the first time
Only staff who failed a phishing simulation
Only directors who chair Board committees
Key personnel in executive, operational and security administration or management roles
bank.explanation: Paragraph 200 requires targeted awareness and training for key personnel in executive, operational and security administration or management roles, on top of general awareness.

bank.question: A manager argues that if his team completed awareness at induction, nobody needs to check what they remember. Which paragraph contradicts him?
options: Paragraph 151, which sets how often vulnerability assessments of critical systems must happen
Paragraph 165, which sets DR drill frequency
Paragraph 182, which sets the DAKSH reporting deadline
Paragraph 202, on evaluating staff awareness periodically
bank.explanation: Paragraph 202 requires periodic evaluation of employees' awareness, and paragraph 197 lets awareness form part of assessing the bank's preparedness.

bank.question: Customers receive SMS links to a page that copies the bank's login screen. Besides warning customers, what external service must the bank already have in place?
options: A CERT-In certificate for its website
A cyber insurance policy that pays every affected customer automatically within one working day
A contract with a newspaper to publish weekly warnings
An external anti-phishing and anti-rogue app takedown service
bank.explanation: Paragraph 148 requires a subscription to anti-phishing and anti-rogue app services from external providers to identify and take down phishing sites and rogue apps.

bank.question: An attacker registers 'godavariharbour-bank.co' and sends staff invoices from it. Which control in paragraph 117 is aimed at this?
options: Annual capacity planning of IT resources
Geographic separation of DC and DR sites
Straight through processing of data between applications
Measures in secure mail systems against email spoofing and look-alike domain abuse
bank.explanation: Paragraph 117 requires secure mail and messaging systems with measures against spoofing, look-alike domain abuse, malicious attachments and links, and spam, and asks partners and vendors to do the same.

bank.question: A fraud ring calls customers posing as the bank and asks them to install a remote access app. Under the Digital Payment Security Controls Directions, what should the bank's mobile app try to do?
options: Report each such call to the telecom provider
Detect remote access apps where possible and block login to the banking app
Ask the customer to uninstall the app permanently
Allow login as normal but cap all transactions at a small amount until the next branch visit
bank.explanation: Paragraph 68(2)(iv) requires mobile apps to be able to identify remote access applications where possible and prohibit login, alongside customer warnings about remote access fraud.

bank.question: Which list of threats appears in RBI's Cyber Crisis Management Plan requirements as attacks banks must prepare for?
options: Only DDoS attacks on the bank's website
Spear phishing, whaling, vishing and business email frauds, among others
Only insider frauds by branch staff
Only physical theft of servers and fire in data centres
bank.explanation: Paragraph 193 lists many threats, including DDoS, ransomware, business email frauds, email phishing, spear phishing, whaling, vishing, identity frauds and password-related frauds.

bank.question: Zoya's staff ask why they should report a phishing mail they did not click. What is the best answer?
options: Reports are needed only so that HR can calculate staff awareness bonuses at the end of the year
Reporting is only required after money is lost
Early reports let the team block the sender and warn others before anyone is hooked
RBI forbids reporting mails that were not clicked
bank.explanation: RBI asks banks to encourage reporting of suspicious behaviour to the incident management team. A report at the lure stage gives the best chance of preventing an incident.

bank.question: Which of these is the bank required to educate customers about under paragraph 61 of the Digital Payment Security Controls Directions?
options: Sharing OTPs only with family members
Keeping a written copy of their PIN with the card
Choosing the cheapest mobile data plan
Keeping devices secure: regular updates, apps only from authorised sources and anti-malware
bank.explanation: Paragraph 61 requires education on physical and logical device security, including regular OS and app updates, downloading apps only from authorised sources and having anti-malware.

bank.question: A customer says he was told by a 'bank officer' on the phone to share his OTP to stop fraud. A teller replies, 'That's normal procedure.' Which bank duty is the teller undermining?
options: Reconciling payments within 24 hours
Educating customers never to share credentials, OTPs or PINs, a message staff must reinforce
Keeping the ITSC chair independent
Maintaining an enterprise data dictionary
bank.explanation: Banks must educate customers about the risks of sharing OTPs and PINs (paragraph 207) and caution them about vishing (DPSC paragraph 64). Staff who call it normal undo that education.

bank.question: Which statement about customer reports of phishing is correct under paragraph 206?
options: The bank must charge a fee to investigate each report
Customers must report phishing only to CERT-In, never to the bank, which has no role in handling such reports
The bank must encourage customers to report phishing mails and sites, and act effectively on them
The bank may ignore reports unless a loss has occurred
bank.explanation: Paragraph 206 requires the bank to encourage customers to report phishing mails and phishing sites and to take effective remedial action on such reports.

bank.question: A core banking DBA needs root access for a patch on Saturday. Which approach best meets paragraphs 105, 108 and 111?
options: Give him a permanent root password so that future weekend patch windows can run without any delays
Time-limited access via the privileged access system, fully logged and reviewed
Let him use a colleague's account if his access is not ready
Share the root password with the whole DBA team for cover
bank.explanation: Elevated access is given for a specific need and duration, managed through centralised controls, with all activity logged and reviewed, and personnel with elevated access closely supervised.

bank.question: Which requirement applies to authentication for administering applications, databases and network devices under paragraph 109?
options: Authentication only for internet-facing devices
Separate local passwords on each device, changed only when a device fails or is replaced by the vendor
Centralised authentication with strong passwords, least privilege and separation of duties
A single shared admin account for each team
bank.explanation: Paragraph 109 requires a centralised authentication and authorisation system for applications, OS, databases, network and security devices, with strong passwords, least privilege and separation of duties.

bank.question: Security monitoring shows a branch user logging in at 3 am from two cities an hour apart. Which RBI requirement makes this worth investigating?
options: Reviewing IT architecture at least annually
Obtaining source code for critical applications
Running DR drills at least half-yearly
Monitoring any abnormal change in the pattern of logon
bank.explanation: Paragraph 113 requires banks to monitor abnormal changes in logon patterns. Impossible travel and odd hours are classic signs of stolen credentials.

bank.question: An auditor needs to copy logs to a USB drive for a one-day review. Which sequence fits paragraphs 121-124?
options: Let the auditor use any drive, because auditors are independent
Allow it if the auditor signs the visitor register
Refuse in every case, because removable media can never be used anywhere in the banking environment
Authorise it for that use and day, scan it, limit what is copied and erase it after
bank.explanation: Removable media is barred by default unless specifically authorised for a defined use and duration; it must be scanned, transfers limited and data securely erased after use.

bank.question: A relationship manager loses a bank laptop holding customer files on a train. Which control in the Directions limits the damage?
options: The data migration policy's sign-off requirement
The ITSC's quarterly meeting
The IPv6 readiness of public-facing systems
Remote management, wiping or locking of mobile devices including laptops
bank.explanation: Paragraph 54 requires controls for remote management, wiping and locking of mobile devices, including laptops, as part of protecting sensitive data.

bank.question: The bank outsources call-centre work to a vendor that stores customer data. Whose duty is it to keep that data confidential?
options: The bank's, as owner of the data, wherever it is stored
Only RBI's, through its inspection of vendors
Only the customer's, once they have consented to the outsourcing in the account opening form
Only the vendor's, once the contract is signed
bank.explanation: Paragraph 53 makes the bank, as owner of customers' personal and sensitive data, responsible for its confidentiality, integrity and availability, whether stored in-house or with third-party vendors.

bank.question: Marketing wants to text a new card offer to all customers using the mobile numbers they gave when opening accounts, without asking them. What should compliance say?
options: Account-opening data needs express permission before cross-selling
It is fine if the texts mask the card number
It is fine as long as the offer comes from the bank itself and not from a third-party company
It is fine because customers gave the numbers to the bank
bank.explanation: Paragraph 63 of the KYC Directions bars using information collected at account opening for cross-selling or other purposes without the customer's express permission.

bank.question: In general terms, how does the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 describe a bank that decides why and how customers' digital personal data is processed?
options: As a significant data processor exempt from breach duties
As a data principal with no duties under the Act
As a consent manager registered with RBI
As a data fiduciary that must protect personal data with reasonable security safeguards
bank.explanation: In the DPDP Act the organisation deciding the purpose and means of processing is the data fiduciary, which must protect personal data with reasonable security safeguards; the person the data is about is the data principal.

bank.question: A ransomware alert is confirmed by the CSOC at 11:30 pm on a Saturday. What is the latest time for the DAKSH report?
options: 9:30 am on Monday, when RBI offices open
5:30 am on Sunday, six hours after detection
11:30 pm on Monday, the next working day after a full day
11:30 pm on Sunday, twenty-four hours after detection
bank.explanation: The six-hour limit in paragraph 182 runs from detection, with no exception for nights or weekends. CERT-In must also be notified proactively.

bank.question: Which statement best describes the relationship between RBI and CERT-In reporting in the 2026 Directions?
options: Report to RBI on DAKSH within six hours and also notify CERT-In
Reporting to CERT-In replaces reporting to RBI
Reporting to RBI replaces reporting to CERT-In
The bank chooses one of the two, depending on whether the incident is a cyber attack or an IT failure
bank.explanation: Paragraph 182 requires both: a DAKSH report to RBI within six hours of detection and proactive notification to CERT-In. CERT-In's own directions also set duties, which this quest does not detail.

bank.question: A vendor managing the bank's ATM switch detects malware on its servers. What should the bank's contract with this application service provider require?
options: The ASP reports only to CERT-In and never to the bank
The ASP must shut down all ATMs nationwide immediately
The ASP informs the bank of incidents promptly and has a written response procedure
The ASP may deal with the incident itself and tell the bank about it at the next contract renewal meeting
bank.explanation: Paragraph 138 requires contracts with ATM switch ASPs to cover incident management, including timely notice to the bank and a written incident response procedure with defined roles.

bank.question: After an incident is closed, the CISO's office updates the response plan with what went wrong. Which requirement does this meet?
options: Dynamically incorporating lessons learnt to continually improve response plans
Hosting the mobile app checksum on a public platform
Annual capacity planning for IT resources
Maintaining a centralised software inventory
bank.explanation: Paragraphs 178 and 187 require banks to incorporate lessons learnt from incidents, tests and drills to keep improving response and recovery.

bank.question: Which arrangement must the bank have on standby according to paragraph 211?
options: A spare Board of Directors ready to take over
Support for network forensics, forensic investigation and DDoS mitigation services
A second regulator's approval for every incident
A public relations firm to deny incidents
bank.explanation: Paragraph 211 requires support or arrangements for network forensics, forensic investigation and DDoS mitigation on standby.

bank.question: In its 2021 penalty on Tamilnad Mercantile Bank, which directions did RBI find the bank had not complied with?
options: The KYC Master Direction's video-KYC rules
The Digital Payment Security Controls Directions, 2026
RBI's 'Cyber Security Framework in Banks' directions of June 2016
The Integrated Ombudsman Scheme, 2021
bank.explanation: The May 2021 press release refers to non-compliance with the Cyber Security Framework in Banks directions dated 2 June 2016, discovered by examining incident reports from October 2019.

bank.question: Which of these must the bank's crisis communication arrangements be tested with, under paragraph 190?
options: Only the media, once a year
Stakeholders including customers and service providers, through periodic drills
Only the bank's internal IT staff
Only RBI officials during inspections
bank.explanation: Paragraph 190 requires periodic drills or tests of the crisis communication plan with stakeholders, including customers and service providers.

bank.question: What does RBI want for the recovery point objective of critical information systems?
options: Near zero, with a documented reconciliation method if it is not zero
Exactly 24 hours of data loss for every system
Whatever the vendor's standard contract offers
No defined value, as RPO applies only to non-critical systems
bank.explanation: Paragraph 171 asks banks to prioritise minimal RTO, approved by the ITSC, and near zero RPO for critical systems; paragraph 172 requires a documented reconciliation method for non-zero RPO.

bank.question: Corporation Bank's 2019 penalty began with an incident report. What did that report concern, according to RBI?
options: A leak of customer data on a public website
Fraudulent transactions carried out with a cancelled debit card
A ransomware attack on the core banking system
Seven fraudulent SWIFT messages worth USD 171 million
bank.explanation: RBI's press release says a cyber security incident report about fraudulent transactions using a cancelled debit card revealed non-compliance with the cyber security and fraud reporting directions, leading to a ₹1 crore penalty.

bank.question: A customer's internet banking access is blocked after too many failed attempts. What do the Digital Payment Security Controls Directions require?
options: Secure re-activation, and telling the customer about the failed attempts
Automatic re-activation after one hour without notice
Re-activation by any branch as soon as the customer telephones and gives his account number
Permanent closure of internet banking for that customer
bank.explanation: Paragraphs 50 and 51 require a set maximum of failed attempts, a secure procedure to re-activate blocked access and notice to the customer of failed attempts.

bank.question: Which internet banking control is specifically required in Chapter IV of the Digital Payment Security Controls Directions?
options: Automatic termination of an online session after a fixed period of inactivity
Passwords sent to customers by ordinary post with no expiry
Unlimited session length for corporate customers
Login only from branch computers
bank.explanation: Paragraph 67 requires, among other things, a virtual keyboard option, automatic session timeout after inactivity and a compulsory change of bank-generated passwords at first login.

bank.question: A customer spots an unknown debit in the bank's app at midnight. What facility must the app provide under paragraph 66?
options: Only a phone number that works during branch hours
A form to download, print and post
A way to flag it as fraudulent in the app for immediate notice to the bank
An option to reverse the transaction instantly by himself, without any checks or authentication
bank.explanation: Paragraph 66 requires a mechanism in mobile and internet banking for customers to mark a transaction as fraudulent for seamless, immediate notice to the bank.

bank.question: Digital banking wants to switch all savings customers to mobile banking by default to boost adoption. What do the Digital Payment Security Controls Directions say?
options: Default enrolment is required by RBI as part of its financial inclusion targets for all savings accounts
Default enrolment is fine for customers under 40
Digital channels only at the customer's option, on a specific request
Default enrolment is fine if customers can opt out later
bank.explanation: Paragraphs 62 and 65 require digital channels to be offered on the customer's express willingness, not bundled without their knowledge, and only on a specific written or authenticated electronic request.

bank.question: How often must the CISO place a review of cyber risks and preparedness before the Board, the Risk Management Committee or the ITSC?
options: At least once every month
At least once every quarter
Only after a reportable incident
At least once every year
bank.explanation: Paragraph 28(7) requires the CISO to place a review of cyber risks, arrangements and preparedness before the Board, RMCB or ITSC at least quarterly.

bank.question: An RBI examiner asks which indicators the bank uses to measure its cybersecurity programme. Which answer matches paragraph 194's illustrations?
options: Number of vendors and their annual turnover
Number of press releases issued and social media followers
Branch footfall and deposit growth
Anti-malware coverage, patch latency, extent of user awareness training and vulnerability metrics
bank.explanation: Paragraph 194 asks for KPIs and KRIs; its examples include anti-malware coverage and update rate, patch latency, extent of user awareness training and vulnerability-related metrics.

bank.question: VA/PT of the internet banking platform found high-risk vulnerabilities. Which follow-up does the Directions require?
options: Accept them automatically if the vendor wrote the code
Fix them on a deadline and report closure to the ITSC and ISC quarterly
Wait for the next annual IS audit to decide whether the vulnerabilities are serious enough to fix
Hide them from senior management until fixed
bank.explanation: Paragraph 153 requires time-bound fixing of identified vulnerabilities, paragraph 160 close monitoring by IS audit and senior management, and paragraph 161 quarterly closure status to the ITSC and ISC.

bank.question: Which pattern links RBI's actions against Union Bank (2019), BBK India (2022) and Kotak Mahindra Bank (2024)?
options: Each involved a breach of the Digital Personal Data Protection Act reported to the Data Protection Board
Each was a criminal conviction of the bank's CISO
Each followed RBI scrutiny of the bank's IT or cyber framework that found gaps
Each was based only on customer complaints to the RBI Ombudsman
bank.explanation: Union Bank's penalty followed fraudulent SWIFT messages, BBK's an IT examination and a reported incident, and Kotak's restrictions RBI's IT examinations. All found gaps in the cyber or IT risk framework; none was a criminal case or DPDP action.
